clue.text: Box of tape stuck in station in India

indicators.note: the word in tells us the second piece is put inside the first

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social station in India
set means stuck fast or solidified

explanation.surface: A box of recording tape has got jammed somewhere at a railway station in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' suggests trains, but here it means social rank in the Hindu system; 'in' places the second piece within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a small plastic case holding magnetic recording tape.

clue.text: Heartbroken states in the spring, classically?

parts.note: the word heart broken up, its letters rearranged
the USA is the United States

explanation.surface: Lovelorn American feelings expressed in springtime, old-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartbroken' is one word holding both fodder HEART and its anagram signal 'broken'. Arethusa was a nymph turned into a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the nymph Arethusa became a fountain in Sicily.

clue.text: Science article on noise of birds from Norway, for example

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation for science
an is the indefinite article
a din is a loud noise
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: A scientific paper about birdsong from Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is one of the Nordic countries, so a Norwegian belongs to that northern region.

clue.text: Poet's profit sent up by city issue

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: net is profit after costs
NY is New York city
issue means offspring, a son

explanation.surface: A poet's earnings mocked by a city publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' looks like 'mocked' but turns NET into TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Record one does break, in the event

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: break signals the letters being broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A record player that does break down, if it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges DOES into SODE.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single incident or occurrence in a series of happenings.

clue.text: Screw up legislator in procedure

indicators.note: in shows one piece placed inside the other

parts.note: a rule is a set procedure
an MP is a Member of Parliament, a lawmaker

explanation.surface: Mess up a politician within the rules of procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw up' looks like wordplay but is the definition: to crumple.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumple or crease is to screw up cloth or paper.

clue.text: Players to toss

explanation.surface: Actors throwing something.
explanation.definitionFit: The performers in a play are its company, and to throw something is also to fling it.

clue.text: College girl's opening much-translated Bible

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a type of college

indicators.note: opening picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: a lot means much

explanation.surface: A student's start on a heavily translated Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: A polyglot Bible prints the text side by side in several languages.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot edition gives the scripture in parallel versions in many languages.

clue.text: Best receptacle round a plant

parts.note: a plum job or role is the best one going
a bag is a container, something that receives things
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A top-quality container is placed around a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is a flowering shrub, also called leadwort, often grown for its blue blossoms.

clue.text: Wife of Zeus caught in the rat race

indicators.note: the letters are trapped across the words that follow, held within them

explanation.surface: The wife of a Greek god finds herself stuck in the daily corporate grind.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'tHE RAt'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hera, queen of the gods, was married to Zeus.

clue.text: Most attractive variety of London Pride?

explanation.surface: The loveliest kind of a famous London beer or plant.
explanation.walkthrough: London Pride is a saxifrage plant (and a British beer); one of its old names is the phrase meaning nothing is lovelier.
explanation.definitionFit: As a phrase it says nothing else is as lovely; it is also a folk name for a saxifrage garden plant.

clue.text: Alien men, green, and touchy at first, being put at risk

indicators.note: alien means strange or foreign, so the letters become strange
at first takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Green aliens, a bit touchy, are threatened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' looks like a noun but rearranges MEN GREEN AND into ENDANGERMEN, then T.
explanation.definitionFit: Endangerment is the state of being exposed to danger or harm.

clue.text: Nothing breaks even in this game!

indicators.note: breaks means one piece splits the other open and sits inside it

parts.note: to be quits is to be even, owing nothing
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a zero score spoils a level result in some game.
explanation.walkthrough: Put O inside QUITS. The game is tossing rings at a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits is a pub and garden game of throwing rings over a peg.

clue.text: Fear 'flu outbreak that is alarming?

parts.note: dread is great fear

indicators.note: an outbreak suggests the letters breaking out of order

parts.note: an old spelling of flu, used as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fear of an influenza epidemic is frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the old spelling is ignored; 'outbreak' plays on an epidemic while signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frightful or terrible is alarming in the same way.

clue.text: Italian dish to droop in the country way

indicators.note: the word in signals one piece going inside the other

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road in the countryside
to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: An Italian dish is made to wilt in the rural manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' looks like 'manner' but is a road, and 'in' sets the droop inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a baked Italian pasta dish of layered sheets and sauce.

clue.text: Lack of energy left the gray spavined

indicators.note: spavined means lame and broken down, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Tiredness that left the lame grey horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A spavined horse is lame from a swollen hock, so the word signals a broken-down arrangement; 'gray' is the American spelling of grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is sluggish weariness, a want of vigour.

clue.text: Conspicuous end of the pit not emptied

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside letters, leaving only the outer pair

explanation.surface: A notable part of the coal pit has not been cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: E (end of 'the') + MINE + NT ('not' with its middle removed).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eminent stands out above others, prominent and noticeable.

clue.text: To feel absence of stimulation, say, is other-worldly

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken

parts.note: to miss is to feel the absence of something, and a tickle is a light stimulation

explanation.surface: Feeling a lack of excitement is somehow spiritual.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS TICKLE spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystical things belong to a spiritual realm beyond ordinary experience.

clue.text: Now is the winter of our discontent (Thomas Hood)

definitions.text: Now is the winter of our discontent (Thomas Hood)

parts.words: Now is the winter of our discontent (Thomas Hood)
parts.note: Shakespeare's line misattributed to Thomas Hood, whose poem lists all the things that are missing in a gloomy month before naming it

explanation.surface: A famous Shakespeare quotation wrongly credited to the Victorian poet Thomas Hood.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood's poem No! lists 'No sun, no moon...' and ends by naming the month; the clue borrows Richard III's gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood's poem names this dreary late-autumn month as the time of no sun, no warmth, no joy.

clue.text: Engage in French offensive

parts.note: en is French for in
gross means coarse or offensive

explanation.surface: Join battle in a French attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like a military attack but means GROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross is to occupy someone's attention fully.

clue.text: Sir Walter's novel charm?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Scott novel is a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Scott wrote a crusader novel with this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's 1825 novel is The Talisman; a talisman is also an object thought to bring luck or ward off evil.

clue.text: Attractive bar, possibly, in which the Famous Five appeared?

definitions.text: in which the Famous Five appeared?

explanation.surface: A charming pub perhaps, featured in children's adventure stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magnet was a British boys' weekly paper whose Greyfriars stories starred Harry Wharton and friends, nicknamed the Famous Five.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar magnet pulls iron toward it; The Magnet was also the old boys' weekly featuring Greyfriars School.

clue.text: Create space for books put on one side

explanation.surface: Making room on the walls for books and setting something aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit shelving gives books somewhere to stand; to postpone a plan is also to lay it aside.

clue.text: Vagrant maids, perhaps, in experimental movement

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged differently

explanation.surface: Homeless servants taking part in some experimental art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks VAGRANT MAIDS as fodder for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Avant-gardism is the practice of radical, innovative art ahead of its time.

clue.text: Vessel taking a right turn

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A ship makes a right turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like steering but is a turn in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth.

clue.text: Famous place of retreat for the Spanish bachelor

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
BA is a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A well-known holiday hideaway for an unmarried Spaniard.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'retreat' is Napoleon's exile in 1814.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to this Mediterranean island after his first abdication.

clue.text: Capone's men with no name as comedians

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: Al Capone led a gang of gangsters

explanation.surface: Al Capone's mob, unnamed, recast as comics.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove N from GANGSTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gagsters are joke-tellers, people who make gags.

clue.text: Advantageous to have trade union backing in salary package

indicators.note: the word in shows one piece placed within the other

parts.note: a salary package is the salary paid

indicators.note: backing means the letters go back to front

explanation.surface: A union's support in pay negotiations is beneficial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but turns the union's abbreviation round, and 'in' places it within the pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something salutary is beneficial or wholesome in its effect.
